ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, a linear function, $y=-x-2$, intersects with the graph of $y=kx+b$ at point $P\left(2, n\right)$. What then is the solution set of the inequality $kx+b<-x-2$ in terms of $x$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: \textbf{Solution:} From the graph, it is known that when $x<2$, the graph of the line $y=kx+b$ is below the graph of the line $y=-x-2$. Therefore, the solution set of the inequality $kx+b<-x-2$ with respect to $x$ is $\boxed{x<2}$.
